newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: AIB shares up 11 Irish pence after U.S. buy.
newsitem.headline: AIB shares up 11 Irish pence after U.S. buy.

text.p: Allied Irish Bank's share price rose 11 Irish pence to 418 pence in early trade following the overnight announcement that it had bought U.S. Dauphin Deposit Corp, dealers said.
"The market is taking the acquisition as a very positive move for the bank. I see the share price going further on the day," one dealer said.
"They bought the bank they wanted to buy and they got it at a good price without recourse to shareholders," one banking analyst said.

"The acquisition is going to be earnings neutral in the current year, modestly earnings enhancing in 1998 and significantly earnings enhancing in 1999 and that is based on very conservative assumptions of revenue growth."
Allied Irish Bank announced late on Tuesday that its U.S. unit First Maryland Bancorp had agreed to buy Dauphin Deposit Corp for $1.36 billion, the biggest acquisition ever made by an Irish company.
